text:
lena: FYI deploybot auto-sticky-pinned runtime-5.0 for qna-plus after a cluster of OOMs in nightly batches. Need a quick scoped-unpin plan for the 02:00 UTC window.

deploybot: [automated] sticky pin applied. pin_id=pb-2026-03-04-03. Affected: model-group 'qna-plus' (qna-xl, qna-fast). Trigger: OOM spikes >3% over 10m. See internal pin page.

ben: telemetry shows issues primarily on long-context batch jobs; interactive short queries look stable. Recommend exclude dedicated pools and batch routes.

arjun: can we do header-tagged canary traffic so logs and traces are easy to query? something like `X-Unpin-Canary:pb-2026-03-04-03`. Also limit to max_seq<=4096 for canary.

sara: agree. Ops: suggested command and rollback criteria?

ops-sre-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pinning. Suggested canary command:
`deploybot unpin --pin pb-2026-03-04-03 --scope region:eu-central --traffic-filter "max_seq<=4096 AND route:!=dedicated AND route:!=batch" --request-headers "X-Unpin-Canary:pb-2026-03-04-03" --mode canary`
Rollback criteria (within 20m): oom_rate >0.5% OR crash_rate increase >1pp OR p95 latency > baseline * 1.2 -> immediate `deploybot pin --pin pb-2026-03-04-03 --force`.

lena: schedule proposal: canary 02:00 UTC -> monitor 20m -> decision 02:25 -> expand 02:45 -> full unwind by 04:00 if green. Sara please update release notes with pin id and exclusions.

sara: on it. Draft note: "Temporary sticky pin pb-2026-03-04-03 on runtime-5.0 for qna-plus due to OOMs on large batch/long contexts. Scoped canary unpin planned; dedicated and batch routes excluded."

ben: I'll run a lightweight synthetic job against canary hosts and tag with the header. Will post the script.

arjun: I'll add ephemeral dashboards and an alert `pin_unpin_rollback_needed` if oom_rate spikes after unpin.

deploybot: I can schedule the canary at 02:00 UTC and will await channel ack. React with :eyes: to approve.

lena: Approved. :eyes: I'll be on-call for the window.

ops-sre-bot: Ops checklist summarized: tag canary hosts, run canary unpin, run synthetic checks, monitor metrics for 20m, rollback command ready if needed. Keep incident log updated.

ben: synthetic (short): `for i in {1..300}; do curl -s -H "X-Unpin-Canary: pb-2026-03-04-03" "https://canary-eu/api/generate?model=qna-fast&max_seq=1024" > r.$i.json & done; wait; jq -s '[.[]]|{errors: map(select(.status!=200))|length,p95:(map(.latency)|sort)[int(length*0.95)]}' r.*.json`

sara: release tracker updated and CS looped in.

lena: thanks. We'll reconvene with canary results; if we need to re-pin include the exact command used and a short metric snapshot.
